    Thanks Joe, this is brilliant. For some reason I didn't look at renderPlot,

    On Thursday, June 6, 2013 8:04:00 PM UTC-7, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:

     

    Josh Lindsteadt <joshlin...@gmail.com> Jun 07 08:20AM -0700  

    Hey guys, I am still struggling with this. I created assetheight()
    function to calculate the changing height of the plot, but currently it
    says it cannot execute because it is not inside a reactive function. I
    have tried moving the height function around, but without any luck. How
    would I modify the following code to be able to dynamically change the
    height? Thanks.
     
     
    output$riskretPlot <- renderPlot(function(){
    makeAssetPlot()
    }, height=assetheight(), width=800)
     
     
     
    On Friday, June 7, 2013 2:10:42 AM UTC-5, Victor Kryukov wrote:

     

    Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> Jun 07 09:06AM -0700  

    Just need to remove the first "function()" (as renderPlot takes an
    expression, not a function); and then remove the () from assetheight (as
    the height parameter is a function, not an expression).
     
    output$riskretPlot <- renderPlot({
    makeAssetPlot()
    }, height=assetheight, width=800)
     
    It is a little inconsistent, I know.

    Winston Chang <win...@rstudio.com> Jun 07 10:53AM -0500  

    Yes, they're in 0.6.0. Have you updated Shiny on the server to the
    latest version?
     
    Also keep in mind that if the user account holding the app has its own
    version of Shiny, the app will use that version of Shiny instead of
    the system-wide installation of Shiny.
     
    To find out what version you're using, start up R and run:
    packageVersion('shiny')
     
     
    -Winston
     
    On Fri, Jun 7, 2013 at 10:39 AM, Dipika Mukherjee

     

    Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> Jun 07 09:03AM -0700  

    And if you're using Shiny Server in its default configuration then the user
    that actually launches the Shiny app, is the "shiny" user. So you'll need
    to install Shiny as root, or as that user. Here's the easy way to install
    it as root:
     
    sudo su - -c "R -e \"install.packages('shiny', repos='
    http://cran.rstudio.com/')\""

 Dynamic forms issue
    stratos mos <soj...@gmail.com> Jun 07 03:28AM -0700  

    Well hi there.I'm so confused trying to implement the following:
    i want to have a form that initially shows a question from a db table,
    while in the bottom of this form there are radiobuttons with labels
    option1,option2 and a submit button.So, when a user chooses option1 another
    question is reactively presented in the same form. Two problems so far:
    1)how can i "hide" the first question that initially is presented and be
    replaced by the next questions
    2)when the user gets the new questions the radiobuttons should be
    reactively some kind of reseted.
     
    *lets say more clear: we must have a form that is reactively re-produced
    exactly how it was and reseted to selected=false.
    Any ideas of how that could be solved?i think that this issue will solve a
    lot of things for building dynamic forms->dynamic reports...

     

    Winston Chang <win...@rstudio.com> Jun 07 09:48AM -0500  

    > 1)how can i "hide" the first question that initially is presented and be
    > replaced by the next questions
     
    There are two options here: You can either use dynamic UI to replace
    the item, or you can use conditionalPanel to hide the item.
     
    For an example of dynamic UI, see here:
    http://glimmer.rstudio.com/winston/dynamic_ui/
     
    For an example of conditionalPanel, see the example on the main Shiny
    page. If you check "Show density estimate", a slider appears at the
    bottom:
    http://www.rstudio.com/shiny/
     
     
     
    > 2)when the user gets the new questions the radiobuttons should be reactively
    > some kind of reseted.
     
    In the new (0.6.0) version of Shiny, you can set the value of
    radioButtons with updateRadioButtons(). The help page for that
    function has an example of how to use it.
     
     
    -Winston

     

 Poor man's persitence
    Dieter Menne <menne...@googlemail.com> Jun 07 06:00AM -0700  

    Take the standard 06_tabsets; when the user is on page "Summary" and asks
    for a refresh, I would like to return to that tab, instead of plot.
     
    Since this is for a single-user application, the current tabset in global
    would be ok, but how do I activate the tabset per code?
     
    Dieter

     

    Winston Chang <win...@rstudio.com> Jun 07 09:35AM -0500  

    Hi Dieter - in the new version that was just released (0.6.0), you can
    use updateTabsetInput, like this:
     
    updateTabsetPanel(session, "mytabset", selected = "panel2")
     
    You'll want to be careful about storing it in a global variable,
    though. Globals are shared across all user sessions, so you'll have to
    make sure that one user's information won't interfere with another.
     
    -Winston

 isolate problems
    Daniel Bowen <count...@gmail.com> Jun 07 06:51AM -0700  

    I believe this is just my lack of understanding with actionButton and
    isolate().
     
    ui contains:
     
    numericInput("number", "Number")
    actionButton("clickhere", "click here")
     
     
    server contains:
     
    library(RMySQL)
     
    conn <- dbConnect(<conn args>)
     
    send_query <- reactive({

    input$clickhere

    isolate(dbSendQuery(conn, paste('SELECT * FROM table WHERE number =',
    number)))

    })
     
    ... I just want the query to run when I click the 'click here' button.
     
    Thank you, in advance.
     
    Dan

     

    Daniel Bowen <count...@gmail.com> Jun 07 07:03AM -0700  

    ... to clarify a bit, nothing happens when I click the "click here" actionButton - no errors, just nothing.
     
    Like I said, I think this is just a lack of understanding on my part. I haven't been able to wrap my head around the actionButton/isolate implementation yet.

     

    Winston Chang <win...@rstudio.com> Jun 07 09:29AM -0500  

    I think you need to put it in observe() instead of reactive(), or you
    need to call send_query() from a reactive endpoint. If you have a
    reactive expression that isn't used by any reactive endpoints, it
    won't be called. You can test this by putting a print statement in
    there.
     
    A reactive endpoint is something that's in observe(). Additionally, if
    you assign a reactive expression to an output, as in `output$foo <-
    reactive( ... )`, it gets wrapped into an observe() under the hood.
     
    This explained in more depth at
    http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#reactivity-overview
     
    -Winston
